has no answer for one. What it cannot know is WHY it was handed one. A swallowed
neighbour rides in `preceding` rather than as a span member -- the comment above the
backward-widening guard says why, and that as a member it would be "emitted correctly
and accounted nowhere" -- so `moved_instruction` offers it to `lower_vex`, which is the
only lowering a carried instruction is ever offered. The span emission lowers 256-bit
perfectly well and never sees it.

The reason now names that. It is the only change kept from this item.

#### What the borrowed wording cost

Two narrowings, each measured and each wrong:

    a member has no span shape      33 of 36 windows have one for every member
    the window was built as plain   all 39 are `unit`

The second needed Finding 314's strategy column to settle, and the first cost a 400-line
probe. **A reason that describes the callee's situation rather than the caller's is
worth less than one that is merely true**, because the reader's next question is always
"how did it get here".

The diagnosis fell out in one step once the strategy was in the roll: for a back-widened
window `window_start = before_address`, so the site the roll names IS the carried
instruction, and all three sampled are 256-bit VEX -- `vmovups (%rcx),%ymm5`,
`vmulps %ymm3,%ymm3,%ymm0`, `vmulps %ymm3,%ymm0,%ymm1`.

#### Refusing the widening instead was measured and reverted

The obvious fix is to refuse a 256-bit neighbour where the guard already refuses EVEX,
one line up, and for the same reason: `moved_instruction` is the only thing that will
lower it and it cannot. Measured:

    frontier                                   996 ->  996      0 left, 0 arrived
    refused stubs                               39 ->    0    -39
    lost to a refused stub                      17 ->    0    -17
    never a candidate                            4 ->    0     -4
    lost to an overlap                          15 ->    6     -9
    declined: 256-bit: arithmetic rather than a copy  31 -> 57  +26
    windows not placed                         443 ->  469    +26

**Not one site was lowered.** The 39 refusals went to zero and the 30 sites moved
sideways. Reverted, and the revert proved byte-identical to the pre-change image.

Three reasons, and the third is the one that decided it:

- **It gains nothing and costs 26 windows.** The narrower window is a real loss in the
  window economy even though the frontier is flat.
- **The new labels are LESS precise.** The 26 that moved are 10 `vdivps`, 5 `vsubps`,
  5 `vaddps`, 3 `vorps`, 1 `vmulps` all-distinct, one aliased `vmulpd` and one
  `vcvtdq2ps` -- every one a shape this tool already lowers, through `lanereg3`,
  `lanealias` and `LANE_UNARY`. Calling them "arithmetic rather than a copy" blames the
  arithmetic, which is not the problem. This file has paid for an imprecise bucket three
  times (310, 314, and the fallback that produced 310); a fourth is not worth a tidier
  refusal count.
- **It is a diagnostic regression.** `stub-refused.txt` is what made this class visible
  at all. Emptying it moves the information into the census under a vaguer name, so the
  roll that found the item would no longer find it.

#### The fix for the imprecision was itself imprecise, twice

**First it flattened the reasons it should have left alone.** Tested on the width and
placed before the re-label, it swallowed `the FMA would not lower` and `no direct SSE
form and not a sequence` as well: three of the 39 traded a reason naming the family for
one naming only the width. 36 + 2 + 1 became 39, and the roll is what showed it. Only
the generic reason is re-worded now.

**Then the repair double-counted.** Popping the generic reason can leave the inner
counter empty, and an `else` on it fired a second `the VEX neighbour would not lower`
for the very refusals just recorded -- 39 reasons over 39 stubs would have become 78.
It is a tally now, because the fallback exists for a `lower_vex` that refused and said
nothing, which is a third case and wants counting rather than inferring from emptiness.

Both were caught by a control over `moved_instruction` directly rather than by a
twenty-minute image run:

    generic 256-bit   reasons=1  the swallowed neighbour is 256-bit ...
    256-bit FMA       reasons=1  the FMA would not lower            kept
    256-bit permute   reasons=1  no direct SSE form and not a sequence  kept
    128-bit           reasons=0  lowered

**This is worth more than the finding it belongs to.** The whole item reverted a change
for making labels less precise, and the replacement did the same thing on its first two
drafts. Precision about a diagnostic is not a thing one is careful about once.

#### The kept change is inert by construction, and is not exercised by any fixture

The lowering `reasons` Counter is written at 47 sites and read at none -- the one
apparent read is a different local, a list of stale-read tuples -- so a reason string
cannot reach emission. Confirmed rather than argued: the image is byte-identical.

**No fixture produces the new wording.** Only Starfield does, 39 times. That is
`evidence.md`'s unproduced-diagnostic hazard, and it is recorded rather than waved past:
a fixture would need a dense 256-bit run with a unit window widening backwards into it,
which is buildable and is its own piece of work.

#### Where it leaves the next item

The 26 sites have working shapes and no strategy claims their window. So the question is
not how to lower 256-bit arithmetic -- Findings 284, 300 and 312 did that -- but **why
no span or unit takes a window in a dense run of 256-bit instructions.** That is the
same question as the 469 unplaced windows and the 506-site withheld class, which is now
over half the frontier and the only large number left.

### Finding 314 -- a roll that could not answer the question it was written for

`repair-blame.txt` carried a window's first byte and a reader's address. A window is a
RANGE and a reader is a SITE, so a reader that is a mid-window passenger could not be
attributed to the window holding it -- and a walk up the blame graph stopped at any
reader that was not itself a window start.

437 of the 443 blamed starts are frontier sites and 65 of that class's sites are
passengers, so the closure was wrong by exactly those. It reported **no cycles at all**
and 443 windows depending on something outside the blamed set, which is not a finding:
it is what a walk that cannot follow an edge prints.

**This is Finding 310's defect for the third time in this file** -- keying on a start
where an extent is meant -- and this time it was in the DIAGNOSTIC rather than in the
census, which is worse. A census bucket that is wrong gets quoted; a roll that cannot
answer its own question **reads exactly like a roll that answers it and finds
nothing.**

The roll carries `width` and `end` now, `end` as a byte address rather than an
instruction count so a consumer can map a reader to a window without parsing the
listing -- which was costing four minutes a question.

#### What the closure says once it can follow an edge

    readers falling inside SOME blamed window   1,126 of 1,141
      of which inside the window they blame        63
    readers outside every blamed window            15

**98.7% of the blame is internal to the withheld class.** The ranking inverts with it:

    class                                  sites  only  gain   per
    lost to a refused stub                    17   103   120   7.1
    declined: 256-bit: arithmetic              31    45    76   2.5
    lost to an overlap                        15    50    65   4.3
    declined: no SSE form at any register      6     0    19     -

`no SSE form at any register` is the one the broken walk would have picked. It is
terminal for 156 chains from six sites, which looks like the highest leverage in the
tree -- and **no window depends on it alone**, so releasing it releases nothing by
itself. An edge count is not a lever, and only a closure that follows extents can tell
them apart.

#### The strategy column refutes what the reason implied

`moved: 256-bit, no Y strategy took it` comes from `lower_vex`, the per-instruction
fallback, so the obvious reading is that the window was built as `plain`. Recorded:

    strategy of the 39 refused stubs    39 unit

Every one is `unit` -- the strategy that DOES lower 256-bit. So a member inside a unit
window is falling through to the per-instruction path, which is a different defect from
the one the reason suggested and is where the next item is. Two earlier measurements had
already narrowed it wrongly: 33 of the 36 windows have a span shape for every member,
so the classifier is not the cause either.

#### The control for an instrument is that the artifact does not move

    apply rc=0
    IDENTICAL

Byte-identical to the Finding 313 image, 112,536,064 bytes. A diagnostic change that
alters the output is not a diagnostic change, and nothing else in the run would have
said so.

The extent was checked against the listing rather than believed: window `0x140001032`,
width 9, end `0x140f91807` in the Starfield roll and width 8, end `0x14000105c` in the
`repairdrop` fixture -- eight instructions, two of the listing lines being encoding
continuations rather than instructions, and the ninth beginning exactly at the recorded
end.

### Finding 313 -- padding says where a function ends, an entry point where one begins

`chunks` splits the code outside `.pdata` at `int3`, and that finds where a function
ENDS. Between two described functions MSVC leaves no padding at all: it packs several
leaf functions and their embedded constants there. So one chunk spans the lot --
entered at its first byte, holding the constants as `(bad)`, and ending wherever the
next described function starts rather than at a `ret`.

Classified whole it fails three of the four conditions at once, and 319 surviving sites
went with it: the largest class in the frontier.

`split_refused` re-cuts a refused chunk at its entry points and hands each piece to the
same `classify`. That is not a new argument -- a call, jump or `lea` destination is a
true instruction boundary, which is exactly what the second condition already asserts
about a chunk start.

#### What the recut admitted

    frontier                                  1,247 ->   996    -251
      declined: outside .pdata                  319 ->    73    -246
      declined: next instruction will not move  106 ->   101      -5
    leaf ranges in the oracle              38,697 -> 43,553  +4,856
    VEX sites in the oracle                17,237 -> 17,498    +261
    in-place patches                      520,369 -> 520,511    +142

251 left by address and **nothing arrived**. `verify` passes.

#### Three framings were wrong before this one was right

Recorded because each cost a measurement and each looked obviously true:

    the 268 are data, so recount            all 11 chunks entered, ordinary code
    split at (bad), trust the prefix        0 of 268 end in a transfer
    they are mid-function fragments         every chunk lies BETWEEN .pdata ranges

The second is the one worth keeping. Splitting at the `(bad)` and trusting everything
before it admits 268 sites -- and **not one of those segments ends in a control
transfer**, because a segment spans several packed functions and stops where the
disassembler lost its footing. Admitting them would have meant dropping the one
condition that catches a desync which does not announce itself.

#### The first implementation was a hundredfold over-reach

Splitting EVERY chunk turned 3,006 into 108,688 pieces and admitted 14,174 VEX sites,
from a change meant to recover 141. Two properties said so:

    newly admitted pieces 16-byte aligned     71.9%
    refused pieces 16-byte aligned            93.9%
    newly admitted ending in a CONDITIONAL jump  2,216

The alignment inversion is the sharper one: it is the same test `outside.py` used to
validate the original 865 lea-referenced chunks, and it came back pointing the other
way. Both come from cutting genuine functions at their internal loop heads. A chunk
that already passes has nothing to gain from being cut, so only refused ones are.

**A recut piece has lost the first condition, so the third pays for it.** With no
padding either side, "ends in a transfer" carries the whole weight of *this is where
the function ends*, and a conditional jump is exactly where a function does not end.
Requiring a `ret` or unconditional `jmp` costs 9 VEX sites of 142 and drops 236 pieces
of 1,239.

#### The ceiling was wrong by a factor of two, and the reason is the finding

**Predicted 132, measured 246.** The prediction was written down before the run,
together with the note that this class is terminal for zero blame edges so the figure
was a CEILING rather than a floor, and that exceeding it would mean the oracle grew
somewhere unmeasured. It was exceeded, so that check was run: all 246 released sites
inside an admitted range, none outside, which is the answer that matters.

The ceiling was wrong because **the input was reconstructed instead of asked for.**
`leaf_ranges` takes its entry evidence from `detour.analysis_context`'s `blocked` set;
the measurement built its own from `targets.collect` plus `call_targets` plus
`lea_targets`. Those are different sets -- `blocked` carries every direct branch and
call destination scraped from the disassembly and carries **no** `lea` targets -- so
the answer was a true measurement of a set the tool does not use.

    with the reconstructed set   133 of 246 covered, 113 apparently not
    with `blocked`, as apply does    246 of 246 covered

**For a moment the first line read as a correctness fault**: 113 sites released with
nothing vouching for the bytes. It was an artifact of the instrument, and the
instrument was one call away -- `analysis_context` returns `blocked`, and that is what
apply passes. `evidence.md`'s rule about another tree's facts holds inside one tree:
a value you rebuild is a measurement nobody took.

#### And the two entry sets disagree, which is its own finding

`outside.main` reports using `lea_targets`; `detour` builds the oracle from `blocked`,
which has none. So the report and the oracle answer "where does code begin"
differently, and the report is the more generous of the two. `analysis_context`'s own
docstring is about exactly this -- "one construction, because two would drift" -- one
level further out than it was written for.

Not acted on. Adding `lea_targets` to `blocked` would grow the oracle and wants its
own measurement rather than riding along on this one.

#### The control is inside the tool, because nothing else guards this

`outside` is a report target, not a gate, and no suite exercises `classify`. So
`leaf_ranges` runs `control()` before answering, and it refuses with *the control
failed, so no result below means anything*. Its cases are the ones
`split_refused`'s argument needs, and the load-bearing one is a pair: the SAME chunk
accepted whole and refused recut.

Sabotaged by making `classify` stop reading the seventh field, which is how the
distinction would really be lost:

    outside.py: the control failed -- recut, ends in a conditional jump
    was accepted and must be refused. No result below means anything.

Without it, that field falling out of use brings back 236 mid-function pieces and
nothing downstream says so -- the oracle is simply bigger.

### Finding 312 -- the destination is the other source, and the order is kept

`op %ymmD,%ymmS,%ymmD` is the shape where the destination is also the second
source. SSE has no three-operand form, so something has to move first, and
`lower_vex` wants a scratch REGISTER for it. Finding 284 found a way round that
needs none -- exchange the sources and the destination becomes the operand SSE
has room for -- and gated it on `COMMUTATIVE_YMM`, because an exchange is only
sound where the operation commutes.

That left 39 sites in Starfield declining as `256-bit: arithmetic rather than a
copy`, and it left a decision standing with the copyright holder: whether to
commute FP add and multiply, which commute arithmetically but change which NaN
payload propagates.

**The decision is retired rather than answered, and it could never have covered
the class anyway.** Of the 39, only 28 are FP add or multiply. Six `vsub*`, one
`vpsubd` and two `vcmpltps` do not commute at all, so whichever way the question
went, nine sites needed a different lowering.

#### The emission, and why it needs one helper where `lanereg` needs two

    0f 28 e1           movaps %xmm1,%xmm4        save src2's low half
    0f 28 c8           movaps %xmm0,%xmm1        D = src1
    66 0f fa cc        psubd  %xmm4,%xmm1        D = src1 - src2, in that order
    41 0f 10 a3 50 ..  movups 0x50(%r11),%xmm4   H = src1's upper half
    66 41 0f fa a3 60  psubd  0x60(%r11),%xmm4   H = src1 - src2, upper
    41 0f 11 a3 60 ..  movups %xmm4,0x60(%r11)

The low half needs no slot: the helper the span already owns holds the value the
destination is about to lose. The upper half reads the DESTINATION's slot as the
OPERAND, which is the only arrangement available with one register -- the
operation computes `reg OP mem`, so the register has to hold src1 and the memory
operand has to be src2.

`lanereg` spends its second helper on moving that operand into a register
instead. Not spending it is the whole gain: **35 of the 39 sites have no free
register at all**, measured with `find_scratch`, which is why `commuted_piece`
was reached for in the first place.

**The operand order is kept, so the lowering is exact.** No NaN-payload
deviation, and nothing to ask for.

#### It read as impossible, and the sentence that said so was right about the stack

`lanereg`'s comment says this emission was tried and faults:

    The obvious emission is `op slot(%base),%xmmH` ... It faults. A packed
    SSE operation requires its memory operand to be 16-byte ALIGNED, and
    nothing aligns a slot ... The first build of this segfaulted on its
    first run.

And `slot_tail`, which exists to build exactly that address, says it is not safe
as an arithmetic operand and that **nothing uses it today**. Both were written
when the slots lived in the stack, where Win64 guarantees `rsp` only at a call
boundary.

`span_slot_op` contradicts them: it emits packed arithmetic against
`disp32(%block)`, the FMA path uses it, and 400 Starfield stubs carry it. What
resolves the contradiction is that the per-thread block is not the stack -- its
base is the loader's, bound by the alignment the TLS directory declares, and
Starfield declares 16.

So `slot_tail` has its first caller, and the impossibility claim was true of the
backing store it was written against rather than of slots as such. This is
`evidence.md`'s *sweep for claims of impossibility* paying out: the deterrent
was the one with no remedy beside it.

#### The fixtures were passing on the allocator's goodwill

Establishing that alignment turned up a plain defect one layer down:

    struct.pack_into(..., TLS_ZERO_FILL,
                     0x00100000)		# ALIGN_16BYTES

`IMAGE_SCN_ALIGN_16BYTES` is `0x00500000`. The field holds 2^(n-1) in bits
20-23, so `0x00100000` declares ONE byte, under a comment naming sixteen. Every
fixture reading a slot as an arithmetic operand -- the whole FMA family -- was
executing only because wine's allocator happens to return aligned memory.

**The thing meant to prove the mechanism could not fail for the reason the
mechanism can fail.** Starfield declares 16 so the shipped stubs are sound, and
nothing was enforcing that: `slot_arithmetic_safe` does now, `span_slot_op`
consults it, and it **refuses on None** -- an emitter reached before any plan was
made declines rather than emitting against an alignment nobody measured. Its
control is the old one-byte image, which now gets zero slot-operand instructions
and a refusal where the sixteen-byte one gets two and a lowering.

#### What it released

    frontier                                          1,628 -> 1,247    -381
      kept: its window was withheld                     834 ->   502    -332
      declined: 256-bit: arithmetic rather than a copy    72 ->    31     -41
      lost to a refused stub                             22 ->    17      -5
      lost to an overlap                                 16 ->    15      -1
      kept: a repair left it in VEX form                  13 ->    11      -2
    refused stubs                                        57 ->    39     -18
      moved: 256-bit, no Y strategy took it              51 ->    36     -15
    windows not placed                                  752 ->   443    -309

By address: **382 left, 1 arrived.** The 41 that left the class audit to the 39
aliased sites plus two memory-source `vmulps (%rax),%ymm7,%ymm3` that left the
frontier entirely once their windows became placeable.

**The prediction was 226 and the outcome was 381, which is worth recording as a
method error rather than a happy surprise.** The forecast counted 39 sites plus
the 187 blamed windows whose ONLY terminal blamer was this class, and said the
other 295 would move only if their other terminals cleared too. They largely
did, because those terminals were themselves in this class or reachable through
it. **A single walk of a blame DAG gives a floor, not an estimate** -- the
transitive closure has to be taken over the whole released set at once, not per
window.

#### The one site it cost

`0x142dcb620 vaddps %ymm2,%ymm0,%ymm4` is all-distinct, was being lowered, and
now declines. It is not in the refusal roll: it is a passenger inside a window
starting four bytes earlier at `0x142dcb61c`, eight instructions wide, refusing
for `moved: 256-bit, no Y strategy took it`. Window reshaping swept it in. That
reason is now the largest stub refusal at 36 and is where the next item is.

#### Both controls fail through their own check, and the second one numerically

    classifier branch removed     4 sites refused, exit 29
    low half commuted             exit 37

37 is forty below 77, which is 20 minus -20: the fixture watches the operand
ORDER rather than the presence of a lowering. A control that only proved "no
lowering, no pass" would have said nothing about the thing this shape exists to
get right.

#### `check-shadow-pe` refused the fixture, correctly

    check-shadow-pe: lanealias answers 77 without
                     permanent slots, so it never
                     needed them and proves nothing

With no slots the pair strategy splits the fixture through home space and
arrives at 77 by another road, so that gate's A/B cannot speak for this shape.
It lives in `check-pe`, which runs the default, and the discriminating evidence
is the control above. **A gate refusing a fixture for the right reason is the
gate working**, and the note is in the fixture so nobody moves it back.

### Finding 311 -- one mnemonic, two encodings, and a set keyed on the name

`vpsllq` names two different instructions. `0F 73 /6` is the immediate group:
ModRM.reg is an opcode extension, so the destination has nowhere to live but `vvvv`.
`0F F3` is an ordinary NDS three-operand instruction whose shift count is a register,
with the destination in ModRM.reg where it belongs. Nine mnemonics carry both forms.

`DESTINATION_IN_VVVV` is a set of MNEMONICS. Every site of either encoding was routed
to a lowering written for the first, and the second could only refuse.

    c5 e1 f3 c8      vpsllq %xmm0,%xmm3,%xmm1   variable    refused
    c5 f1 73 f1 02   vpsllq $0x2,%xmm1,%xmm1    immediate   lowered

The routing reads the opcode byte now, which is the discriminator, and the ordinary
three-operand path takes the variable form. Checked against `as` byte for byte:
`0f28cb 660ff3c8`, `0f28e2 660ff3e1`, `660f73f102`.

#### The comment beside the set said so

    # ... the shift group mixes NDD immediate forms with NDS register forms
    # under one mnemonic, so telling them apart needs the opcode rather
    # than the name.

That is in `patch.py`, three lines above the set, and it is right. It was written to
explain why the in-place patcher excludes the group WHOLESALE -- a decision that is
correct there, because the patcher only ever declines. The sentence describing the
hazard travelled with the set into a consumer that does not decline, and nothing
carried the instruction not to key on the name.

**So the defect is not that nobody knew.** It is that a set's name says what its
members ARE and cannot say what they must be looked up BY, and the one place that
knew was a comment attached to the definition rather than a property of it.

#### Four other consumers, and only one of them mattered

The set has five readers. Keying on a mnemonic is wrong in all five; it costs
something in two, and the cost differs.

    detour.py:1382   the routing               the finding, fixed
    detour.py:10922  the aliasing test         a lost site, fixed below
    patch.py:373     the in-place patcher      right by its own length test
    scratch.py:422   wants_scratch             unreachable, has_direct_sse_form first
    scratch.py:498   a diagnostic census       unreachable, same guard

`patch.py` separates the encodings without meaning to: it asks whether the operand
list holds exactly two registers, which the immediate form satisfies and the variable
form cannot. It reaches the right answer from the wrong premise, which is worth
knowing rather than tidying -- a test that is accidentally coextensive with the one
you want is a test that stops being so when either side moves.

#### The aliasing test, and an empty cell

The collector asks for a scratch register when a three-operand site's src2 IS the
destination, because the `movaps` that sets up the destination would destroy src2
first. It excluded this set wholesale. For the variable form that exclusion is pure
loss: the count register can alias the destination exactly as any other src2 can, and
the `len(registers) == 3` guard beside it already separates the encodings.

`lower_vex` is right in both directions, which is what makes the cost a lost site
rather than a wrong one:

    scratch=None   ->  None                      refuses
    scratch=xmm5   ->  movaps %xmm3,%xmm5        saves the count
                       movaps %xmm1,%xmm3        then the destination
                       psllq  %xmm5,%xmm3        shifts by the saved count

**Starfield holds none of them.** All 22 of its variable-group sites are the
all-distinct case, so this cell is empty and no measurement can speak for it. Per
`evidence.md` the answer is to assert the partition rather than the cell: `varshift`
carries all three aliasing cases, every one contributing to the sum, so a lowering
that writes the wrong register changes the answer instead of merely assembling.

    all distinct    xmm1 <- xmm3 << xmm0    movaps then shift
    src == dst      xmm4 <- xmm4 << xmm5    patches in place
    count == dst    xmm5 <- xmm3 << xmm5    needs a scratch

#### Both controls fail through their own check

Not "the fixture goes red" -- which of the two changes it goes red for:

    routing by the mnemonic alone      1 refused, exit 29
    the aliasing exclusion restored    1 refused, exit 29, 1 fewer overlap

Each was sabotaged in a COPY of `tool/`, because the Starfield pipeline was mid-run
and would have imported the tree at its next stage. That is the third time this
session a background run has constrained how a control could be taken.

#### What the routing released

    frontier                             1,649 -> 1,628    -21
    lost to a refused stub                  43 ->    22    -21
    lost to an overlap                      16 ->    16    unchanged
    kept: its window was withheld          834 ->   834    unchanged
    refused, the vvvv shift would not lower 22 ->     1

**Exactly 21, and the withheld class did not move.** That was the prediction, written
down before the run reported: 22 variable-group sites counted from `build/text.asm`,
21 of them in the baseline frontier and every one of those as `lost to a refused
stub`. The prediction allowed for less than 21, because these sites already have
windows and placing a window can blame a neighbour into the withheld class. None did.

The bucket lost exactly those 21 and gained nothing, which is the check worth stating
separately from the total: a net of 21 could also have been 25 released and 4 arrived.

    baseline 43, now 22; left 21, arrived 0

`verify` passes, including `no call inside any of 400 TEB save bracket(s)` and `stub
section has 0 VEX instructions`.

**The measured image predated the aliasing fix, so it was re-made and compared.**
`apply` imports at process start, and the run that produced these numbers had been
going for twenty minutes when the exclusion came out of `collect`. The aliasing change
can only reach a shift with three registers and `count == dst`, of which this binary
has none -- but that is reasoning, and the point of the change was that reasoning about
which cell is empty had already been wrong once. Re-run on the committed tool the image
is byte-identical, 112,536,064 bytes, and `the aliased form has no usable scratch`
stands at 1 in BOTH runs, which is what shows that refusal belongs to `vpsubd` rather
than to this item.

#### The one shift that still refuses is not one of them

    0x142d8cf2e  vpsrad $0x10,%ymm1,%ymm2   the vvvv shift would not lower
    0x142d8cf41  vpsubd %ymm2,%ymm1,%ymm2   the aliased form has no usable scratch

Both are 256-bit and neither is the variable form. The first is the IMMEDIATE group at
`ymm` width, which `lower_vvvv_shift` has never handled and which belongs to the Y
strategies rather than here. The second is `vpsubd`, not in the set at all, and its
refusal predates this item.

**Neither appears in the refused-stub bucket**, in either run: the census gives them
`kept: its window was withheld` and `declined: 256-bit: arithmetic rather than a copy`.
A site can refuse a stub and be counted under a different verdict, so **the stub roll
and the census are different denominators** -- 57 refusals against 22 sites -- and
reading one as the other is how the remembered figure of 78 would have been quoted
against a bucket of 43.

#### How the item was found, which is the reusable part

`place_stubs` took a `detail` parameter and nothing passed one. Wiring it to
`build/stub-refused.txt` turned `lost to an overlap or a refused stub` -- itself only
just separated, in Finding 310 -- into a named list, and the second-largest reason in
it was a group of nine mnemonics nobody had looked at. **Three times this session the
next item came from wiring a diagnostic that already existed rather than from
measuring something new.**

### Finding 310 -- a fallback bucket that said the opposite of the truth

`never a candidate` held 31 sites and the name is what made them worth an item: not
"the lowering refuses this" but "the collector never reached a decision". The sites
are ordinary 256-bit three-register arithmetic -- `vdivps %ymm1,%ymm2,%ymm4` ten
times over, `vsubps`, `vaddps`, `vpand` -- shapes the span path lowers by the
thousand.

The collector had seen every one of them.

    lost to an overlap or a refused stub    32 ->  59     +27
    never a candidate                       31 ->   4     -27
    frontier                             1,649 -> 1,649   unchanged

**The total holding exactly is the check.** Nothing is lowered by this; had the
figure moved, the rewriter would have been altered under cover of a relabelling.

#### The defect

The census attributes a survivor against `wanted`, which held candidate START
addresses, while the `inside_dropped` bucket beside it is spread over window
EXTENTS. A window widened backwards begins on the instruction BEFORE its site, so
its site is never a start; it falls past every test into the fallback. Both sets are
spread over their extents now.

#### Why it survived, which is the part worth carrying

**This is Finding 282's defect exactly** -- keying on a start where an extent is
meant. There it put 79 survivors in `unaccounted`, and the census ASSERTS that
bucket is zero, so it was caught at once and loudly. Here the same error landed in a
fallback with no assertion attached, and **a wrong label reads as data**.

So the lesson is not about addresses. It is that a bucket named for the absence of
information -- `never a candidate`, `some other shape`, `no reason given` -- is where
a mis-keyed lookup goes to be invisible, and the only thing that makes such a bucket
honest is an assertion about what may land in it. `unaccounted` has one. This did
not.

An item's whole measurement went on hunting a reason the collector skips sites. It
does not skip them. **Two plausible causes were ruled out before reaching this one**:
the sites are not in the in-place patch set, tested at 0 of 31, and they are not
`(bad)` rows or data-island residents, either of which records a decline.

#### What it changes for picking

`lost to an overlap or a refused stub` is 59, nearly twice what it appeared, and it
is a different KIND of class from a floor: those candidates exist and were lost to
placement rather than refused for want of a lowering.

### Finding 309 -- `--teb-scratch=auto` is the default

Instructed by the copyright holder 2026-09-29. Worth **688 sites**: 2,337 without it
against 1,649 with, both re-measured on the same tool the day the decision was taken
rather than quoted from the table -- which is Finding 305's whole point, and which
this document had already got wrong twice.

    default build, before                     2,337
    default build, after                      1,649
    windows not placed                          752
    repair settled after                    68 of 256 rounds
    scratch displacements                     1,600 in 400 stub(s)

`verify` passes with no flag on the command line, including `no call inside any of
400 TEB save bracket(s)`. **The new default reproduces the flagged build exactly**,
which is the control: a default that did not give what the flag gave would be a
different thing wearing its number.

The gap had been WIDENING -- 341 when Finding 297 raised it, 640 at Finding 305, 688
now -- because every item since depends on the slot machinery the TEB route feeds.

#### Two things a default flip owes, both learned from Finding 295

**A default must be a no-op where the thing it enables is unused.** The auto path
resolved `TlsAlloc`, `GetCurrentProcess` and `TerminateProcess` from the import table
unconditionally, so with `auto` on by default EVERY image would have to import them
to be rewritten at all -- including the dozens of fixtures that deliberately import
nothing. The requirement is gated on there being placeholders to patch. `fmareg`,
which imports nothing, rewrites and answers 77 under the bare default.

**The A/B has to stay reachable.** `--teb-scratch=off` exists now. Every default this
tool has taken kept its predecessor runnable -- `--index-const=off`,
`--shadow-regs=off` -- because a default whose alternative cannot be run is a
measurement nobody can repeat.

`--teb-scratch=<offset>` is now the odd one out: it names bytes in somebody else's
TEB with nothing establishing they are free, which is Finding 280's open half. It
stays reachable and is on no path anyone should take.

#### A stale fixture produced a FALSE FAILURE

`check-verify` failed on `regioncarry` with 6 lost boundaries and a stub clobbering a
register its site was using. It is not a defect: `build/sse-regioncarry.exe` was
stale, `make` thought it current, and removing it and rebuilding gives an image
byte-identical to a fresh apply which verifies with zero failures.

**`build-and-commit.md` names this rule and names it for the other direction.** Never
conclude a test passes from a binary the build step did not rebuild -- and the
failure mode assumed is a false PASS. This was a false FAILURE, which is the cheaper
half of the same defect only because somebody happened to chase it; a session with
less patience reverts a correct change instead.

**The mechanism is not established and is written down as unestablished.** The
artifact's mtime was newer than `tool/detour.py`'s, so `make` was right by the rule
it applies; what is not explained is how a build from that pair differs from a build
from the same pair hours later. `regioncarry` is the only fixture affected, it is the
only one that places a region, and Starfield emits no regions at all -- so nothing in
the shipping path depends on the answer, and the honest record is the observation
rather than a mechanism nobody measured.

### Finding 307 -- the variable blend, and the avalanche running forwards

`vblendvps` was the largest root blamer left: 14 blamers, 31 windows blamed only by
them, every one of those windows a singleton. It had no shape at all -- four ymm
operands, `span_operand_shape` returning None, the sites refusing as `shape four
operands` -- and SSE4.1's `blendvps` reads its mask only from the implicit `xmm0`.

    frontier                                  1,820 -> 1,649     -171
      kept: its window was withheld             979 ->   834     -145
      declined: no SSE form at any register      19 ->     6     -13
      kept: a repair left it in VEX form         21 ->    13      -8
    windows not placed                          889 ->   752     -137
    four operands refusals                       28 ->     0
    unconditional lowering refusals             274 ->   174

`verify` passes, including the invariant this emission most needed: it writes `xmm0`
and gives it back twice per member, and no stub clobbers a register its site was
still using across 202,098 placed windows.

**171 sites, and 137 windows released against a bound of 31.** The first time the
realised release has EXCEEDED the bound rather than falling short of it. Those 31
were windows blamed only by `vblendv`; freeing them evidently released readers whose
own windows then placed, and so on -- the avalanche running forwards. Finding 305
measured that 81% of withheld windows are collateral and each root blamer is worth
about five windows; this is the first item to actually collect that, and it collected
four times its bound.

So the instrument's bound is not an upper bound at all. It bounds the FIRST-ORDER
release and says nothing about the cascade, which can run either way: Finding 303
lost nine windows to it and this gained a hundred.

#### Four slots, and a fourth field

The shape needs the destination's slot, both sources' and the mask's -- one more than
anything else. Threading a fourth through the member tuple was two edits, the tuple
having exactly one construction site and one unpack.

#### `xmm0` is SRC1 at every site, so the save comes first

    vblendvps %ymm4,%ymm1,%ymm0,%ymm1      all fourteen look like this

Refusing whenever `xmm0` is involved would have refused every one. The save goes
first and each operand then reads from the saved copy, which is what makes `ymm0`
being a source harmless. Finding 100 paid for the other direction of this mistake:
offering only `xmm0` as the scratch refused 600 `vblendv` sites with a register they
could never use.

`blendvps src,dst` keeps `dst` where the mask is clear and takes `src` where it is
set, so the destination must START as SRC1 -- which is why the accumulator is the
helper and not the destination register.

#### Two things measured rather than reasoned

**The fixture was the unrepresentative thing, not the sites.** With `ymm4` as the
mask -- faithful to the real sites -- the emitter was left ONE free helper and
refused; the probe said `helper=5 second=None`. That looked like the sites being
register-starved. They are not: `blendv wants a second helper` never appears once in
Starfield's refusals. The fixture's tiny function is what has no registers, and the
mask was moved to `ymm2` with the reason written beside it.

**`blendv destination is xmm0` was a guard standing in for an ordering question.**
Four refusals. When D IS `xmm0` its old value is dead, so restoring it and then
overwriting it is two wasted instructions and doing them the other way round
discards the result. `blendv0` fixtures that case.

What still refuses is `cannot borrow xmm0 as a helper`, 2 rows, where the helper
allocation handed back `xmm0` itself.

#### A running measurement broken by an edit

`frontier` returned 1 with a `SyntaxError` at line 182 of a file that parses. The
cause was entirely local: `detour.py` was rewritten while the background run's
interpreter was reading it, so it saw a partial file. **A file rewrite is not
atomic**, and this session routinely has a twenty-minute run in flight while the tool
is edited. The image was rebuilt and the pipeline re-run without touching the tool.

### Finding 306 -- the negated FMA, and what the leverage instrument is worth

`vfnmadd` was the cheap root blamer: 13 blamers holding 17 windows nothing else
blamed. The sequence existed; the gap was that `D = addend - product` cannot
accumulate in one register.

**SSE has no reverse subtract.** The addend must BE the subtract's destination, and
in the upper half the addend is a slot -- so it has to be LOADED while the product
occupies a register of its own. Two helpers, which is why these forms sit outside
`FMA_ONE_HELPER` and take the two `TWO_HELPERS` already allocates for the shape.

    frontier                                  1,838 -> 1,820      -18
      declined: no SSE form at any register      30 ->    19      -11
      kept: its window was withheld             981 ->   979       -2
      lost to an overlap or a refused stub       40 ->    37       -3
    windows not placed                          892 ->   889       -3

`verify` passes. The check that matters for this emission is the stale upper half:
it is the first form to load a slot into a register as the subtract's destination
rather than accumulating in the helper and reading slots as memory, and a wrong slot
address there does not show up as a decode failure.

#### A silent wrong answer the pattern almost allowed

`FMA_PATTERN` puts the negation in its **own capture group**, so the general branch
reads `vfnmadd231ps` as operation `madd` and would have emitted the un-negated
sequence -- correct-looking bytes computing `D + product`. The branch intercepts
ahead of it, and the fixtures are built so the mistake cannot pass: the negated
result has NEGATIVE lanes, `{1..8} - 6` giving `{-5,-4,-3,-2,-1,0,1,2}`, and an
un-negated sequence scores 32 where the fixture wants -4.

`vfnmsub` stays out of the form set: `D = -(product + addend)` needs a sign flip,
which is the construction `lower.py` measured as wrong for NaN payloads.

#### What the blame-edge instrument is actually worth

Four uses, same instrument, three behaviours:

    Finding 300  memory-source FMA    released   0 of 283 predicted
    Finding 303  the RIP immediate    NEGATIVE: 12 lowered, 4 gained
    Finding 304  msubadd              released  28 of  34 predicted
    Finding 306  nmadd                released   3 of  17 predicted

**The SIGN rule holds and the magnitude does not.** Lowering a root blamer has
released windows every time; lowering something that only adds placed windows cost
sites. That distinction is worth keeping and is what picks items.

"Windows blamed ONLY by this class" is an upper bound, and the bound seems to hold
when the class is large relative to the windows it touches and to collapse when it
is small: 13 blamers spread over 17 windows leaves no redundancy, so a window that
acquires any other blamer as the repair re-settles over 60 rounds is simply lost.
Finding 300's zero had a different cause -- a precondition not met, the register-only
half still blaming -- but the shape is the same, a bound quoted as a forecast.

**So state it as a bound with the blamer-to-window ratio attached**, rather than
being surprised by the shortfall each time. Twelve FMA fixtures gate the family now,
one per ordering per shape per operation where a real site exists.

### Finding 305 -- the number that ships was the one nobody re-measured

The auto build was re-measured after every item from Finding 300 to 304. The default
was re-measured after none of them, and none of that work is gated on the flag.

    default build          2,687 -> 2,478      the document said 2,687 throughout
    --teb-scratch=auto     2,346 -> 1,838

**209 sites, quoted wrong for two days**, in the status line at the top of this
document, in the handover table, and in a sentence asserting the default "reproduced
2,687 exactly". That sentence was true when written -- Finding 297 verified it as a
control -- and it stopped being true four findings later, which is the shelf life of
a countable present-tense claim in a document read by lookup.

The tell is worth keeping: **every other number in this arc was re-derived after each
change and this one was re-quoted.** A figure that is measured once and cited
thereafter is indistinguishable from a figure that is measured continuously, right up
until someone re-runs it.

#### And the gap has been widening

    that gap                Finding 297:  341      now:  640

Every item since has depended on the slot machinery the TEB route feeds, so each moved
the auto build further than the default:

                                                  default    auto
    256-bit: arithmetic rather than a copy            632      72
    ymm value has no known upper half                 107       2
    256-bit: no store before 256-bit arithmetic        59       2
    the constant is read by something that will
      not reload it                                    55       -

Without a block pointer that can stand up, sites the slot representation would take
fall back into classes that refuse them. So the standing question -- whether
`--teb-scratch=auto` becomes the default -- is now worth more than every remaining
item put together, and it was worth half this when it was raised.

**It remains the copyright holder's**: it changes what the shipped binary does at load
time, asking the loader for two TLS slots and patching stubs from a callback.

### Finding 304 -- picking by the cascade's SIGN, and msubadd's blend

Finding 303 lowered twelve sites and gained four: it added placed windows without
removing any reader, so nine sites fell back into the withheld class. Findings 300
to 302 gained more than they lowered, because they removed BLAMERS. The difference
is not the size of a class, it is which direction the cascade runs -- and the blame
edges say so in advance.

Of 698 readers holding 920 withheld windows, only **151 are not themselves
withheld**. Those are the sites whose lowering releases anything; a withheld blamer
is circular and releases nothing until something upstream moves.

    vfmsubadd*         14 blamers,  34 windows blamed ONLY by them
    vblendv*           14 blamers,  31 windows
    vfnmadd*           13 blamers,  17 windows
    vptest/vpmovmskb    7 blamers,   7 windows
    F16C                4 blamers,   4 windows
    vmulps 28, vdivps 10, vaddps 8, vsubps 7, vpand 5, vmulpd 5
                                             -- largely the FP-commute decision

#### What it was worth

    frontier                                  1,886 -> 1,838      -48
      declined: no SSE form at any register      44 ->    30      -14
      kept: its window was withheld           1,007 ->   981      -26
      lost to an overlap or a refused stub       46 ->    40       -6
    windows not placed                          920 ->   892      -28

**14 lowered, 28 windows released, 48 net** against a prediction of 14 plus up to
34. That is the closest any leverage estimate in this arc has come, and the reason
is that the item was chosen for its sign rather than its size.

#### The construction is `lower.py`'s, and the instinct was wrong

There is no subadd instruction. The obvious move is to negate the addend and reuse
`addsubps`, since IEEE 754 makes `a - b` and `a + (-b)` the same operation, signed
zeros included. **That is wrong.** The negation is a sign-bit flip across the whole
register, a NaN has a sign bit, and x86 propagates a source NaN with its sign
preserved. `lower.py` records measuring **291 disagreeing vectors in a
special-value sweep, every one a NaN**, the addend coming out `ffc00000` where the
hardware gives `7fc00000`.

Computing both results and blending performs the very add and subtract the hardware
does, so NaN propagation matches by construction -- and it needs no sign-mask
constant, so the rewriter still needs no read-only pool.

    movaps %xmm1,%xmm4          low:  product
    mulps  %xmm2,%xmm4
    movaps %xmm4,%xmm5                copy
    addps  %xmm0,%xmm4                P + D
    subps  %xmm0,%xmm5                P - D
    blendps $0xa,%xmm5,%xmm4          odd lanes from the subtract
    mulps  0x70(%r11),%xmm4     high: the same between slots
    addps  0x50(%r11),%xmm4
    subps  0x50(%r11),%xmm5
    blendps $0xa,%xmm5,%xmm4

It is the one FMA form that does NOT take the one-helper carve-out: the blend needs
both results live, which is the two `TWO_HELPERS` allocates for its shape anyway.

#### Two guards that fired during the work rather than after

`pe_build` refused a **duplicate `cmpconst`** that a copied slice had introduced --
its own check, whose message says a second definition "would silently replace the
first and every gate naming it would keep passing". And the `lanemem` branch would
have matched `msubadd` with a `None` opcode; it refuses instead, because all 14 of
Starfield's are register-only and an emitter with no fixture is what this file
keeps being caught by.

### Finding 303 -- a guard one function away from the bug it was written for

`256-bit: arithmetic rather than a copy` had become the largest non-self class of
blamers: 72 readers holding 94 withheld windows hostage. The label is the `run`
strategy declining anything that is not a load/store copy, and it is not why those
84 sites survive. Cross-referencing all 84 against the refusal roll:

    39 sites  shape a register second source, src2 is D    -- the FP-commute decision
    12 sites  shape a register-to-register move            -- vptest, vpmovmskb
    10 sites  lanemem low half cannot be narrowed          -- this
    12 sites  vcvtph2ps / vcvtps2ph                        -- F16C
     3 sites  lanereg3 wants a second helper
     3 sites  vpermd has no legacy encoding

#### The guard and the bug were in different functions

All ten are `vcmpltps <rip>,%ymm,%ymm`, which carries a compare predicate in an
imm8 after the displacement. `rip_target` refused any tail longer than six bytes:

    if not rip_operand(tail) or len(tail) != 6:
            return None     # an immediate would follow the displacement

**That comment describes arithmetic which does not apply.** The displacement is
measured from the END of the instruction and `length` already counts the immediate,
so a trailing byte changes the target not at all. `rip_operand` has established mod
00 with rm 101, so there is no SIB and the displacement is exactly `tail[2:6]`
whatever follows it.

What the refusal was protecting is `narrow_piece`'s RECONSTRUCTION, which rebuilt
the tail as opcode, modrm and a corrected displacement -- **dropping the
immediate**, turning `cmpps $1` into `cmpps` with whatever byte happened to follow.
That is a real bug and it is one function away. The guard declined a whole class of
instructions to avoid it.

    delta  0: 0f c2 25 58c210fb 01
    delta 16: 0f c2 25 68c210fb 01     displacement +16, predicate intact

`encode_mem` carries the same hazard from the other side -- it rewrites the LAST
four bytes as the displacement, which is only the displacement when nothing follows
it. Nothing reaches it with an immediate today, since no FMA has one, and a silent
corruption is the wrong thing to leave waiting for the first caller that does. It
refuses instead.

#### What it was worth, which is less than the class it fixed

    frontier                                    1,890 -> 1,886      net -4
      declined: 256-bit: arithmetic                  84 ->    72    -12
      kept: its window was withheld                 998 -> 1,007     +9
    windows not placed                            911 ->   920      +9

**Twelve sites lowered and nine came back as newly-withheld windows.** Placing more
windows means more swallowed VEX.128 writes and more blame edges, so windows that
previously placed no longer do. Findings 300 to 302 escaped this because they were
REMOVING blamers; this item adds placed windows and removes no reader, so the
cascade runs the other way. The item is worth four sites, not twelve, and quoting
the -12 on the class it fixed would be quoting the wrong number.

`cmpconst` reads three lanes, one of them in the upper half and true while its
neighbours are false, so a dropped predicate and a dropped upper half each miss.
Restoring the old `!= 6` gives 2 refused and exit 29; the fix gives 77.

#### What remains in the class, and whose it is

39 of the 84 are `src2 is D` on an FP add or multiply -- the decision the copyright
holder already holds. `vmulps %ymm1,%ymm0,%ymm1` has its second source equal to its
destination, and SSE's two-operand `mulps %ymm0,%ymm1` computes the same product,
but **x86 returns the FIRST source's NaN payload**, so commuting changes which NaN
propagates. `COMMUTATIVE_YMM` excludes FP add and multiply for exactly that reason.

When last raised this was 30 sites. Measured with the blame edges it is 39 sites
plus a share of the 94 windows they alone hold. It is a new semantic deviation
rather than an extension of an accepted one -- the FMA rounding rule was already
project policy, this would not be -- which is what keeps it the holder's.

### Finding 302 -- msub and maddsub in a span, and 71 sites that were never the problem

Finding 301 left 123 packed FMA sites in the frontier. Taken as a class that reads
as the next item; broken down by FORM and by REASON it is two different problems:

    madd     71 sites   ALL "kept: its window was withheld"  -- these already lower
    maddsub  14 sites   "no SSE form at any register"
    msubadd  14 sites   "no SSE form at any register"
    nmadd    13 sites   "no SSE form at any register"
    msub     11 sites   "no SSE form at any register"

**71 of the 123 were never a lowering problem.** They lower; their windows do not
place. Spending the item on "123 FMA sites" would have spent most of it on sites
that needed nothing done to them.

#### msub and maddsub

    frontier                                  2,014 -> 1,890
      declined: no SSE form at any register      69 ->    44
      kept: its window was withheld           1,085 ->   998
    windows not placed                          994 ->   911
    unconditional lowering refusals             324 ->   274

**The -25 is exactly msub 11 plus maddsub 14**, the first prediction in this arc to
match to the unit. The other 87 came out of the withheld class: ordinary
instructions in windows released because their last FMA blamer lowered. 83 windows
went, each needing EVERY reader blaming it gone.

`maddsub` is SSE3's `addsubps` -- subtract on the even lanes, add on the odd, which
is VFMADDSUB exactly. `lower.py` has emitted it on the plain path all along and
records having confirmed the lane pattern by RUNNING it rather than by reading the
manual.

#### A bug in code that was already shipped

The 231 low half emitted `addps helper,D`, which is correct **only because addition
commutes**. `subps` and `addsubps` do not. 231 accumulates in the helper and moves
back now, for every operation rather than only the ones that need it: a form that
is right for one operation and silently wrong for the next is worth three bytes to
avoid. All six `madd` fixtures re-pass unchanged.

#### What is declined, and why it is written down

    28  vfmsubadd231ps    no subadd instruction exists
    28  shape four operands
    20  vfnmadd*          D = addend - product cannot accumulate in one helper

**`msubadd` is not register pressure.** The obvious move is to negate the addend
and reuse `addsubps`, since IEEE 754 makes `a - b` and `a + (-b)` the same
operation. That is WRONG: the negation is a sign-bit flip across the register, a
NaN has a sign bit, and x86 propagates a source NaN with its sign. `lower.py`
blends two results instead, which needs a constant. **It records that the error was
caught by `test/fmaddsub_test.c` rather than by reasoning** -- and reading that
paragraph is the only reason this pass did not reimplement the same mistake in the
span path.

#### A roll file that lost its image

`repair-blame.txt` was found at 40 bytes: a `check-pe` run had overwritten
Starfield's 2,889 edges with a fixture's one, and nothing said so. That is Finding
240's rule -- name the image, because the path is fixed -- which
`frontier-sites.txt` has carried for months and which the two files added in
Finding 300 did not. Both carry it now.

**It was caught only because 40 bytes is obviously not an edge list.** A fixture
with a few hundred rows would have read as plausible data, and the next item would
have been picked from a fixture's blame graph.

#### Where the arc ends

2,346 to 1,890 over Findings 300 to 302, and roughly half of the 456 were never FMA
instructions -- they were hostages in withheld windows. That class was called a
floor twice, on two separate measurements, before the blame edges showed it was
waiting on another class.

### Finding 301 -- the register-only FMA, and a class that was waiting on another class

Finding 300 lowered the memory-source FMA and released nothing. The reason was in
its own text: releasing a withheld window needs EVERY reader blaming it lowered, and
71 register-only sites were still blaming. This lowers those, and the windows came.

    frontier                                  2,346 -> 2,014     (Finding 300: 2,279)
      declined: no SSE form at any register     208 ->    69
      kept: its window was withheld           1,227 -> 1,085
      lost to an overlap or a refused stub       83 ->    53
      never a candidate                          54 ->    37
    windows not placed                        1,136 ->   994
    unconditional lowering refusals             606 ->   324

`verify` passes, including the two this change had to clear: every instruction in
the stub decodes, and no surviving 256-bit read takes a stale upper half.

**The 142 that came out of the withheld class is the result, not the 332.** Those
are not FMA sites. They are ordinary instructions in windows that could not be
placed because an FMA reader downstream still needed the zeroing a swallowed
VEX.128 write would have done. **That class was called a floor twice, on two
separate measurements, and it was not closed -- it was waiting on a different
class.** Nothing in the census's own layout could show that; only the blame edges
could.

Realised release is 144 windows against a predicted 283, which the edge data had
already implied: 506 windows carried at least one FMA blamer and only 283 carried
nothing else, and some of that 283 acquired other blamers as the repair re-settled
over 60 rounds.

#### `lanereg3`, and one helper where the shape says two

`vfmadd231ps %ymm3,%ymm2,%ymm4` classifies as `('lanereg3', D, S2, S1)`, which is
not in `SLOT_SHAPES` at all -- so it was refused by the FIRST condition, before the
FMA clause Finding 300 opened. Its upper half has three slots in play where the
memory form had two.

It still wants **one** helper, because two of the three are read as addresses:

    movaps %xmm1,%xmm4          low:  helper = S1
    mulps  %xmm2,%xmm4                helper *= S2
    addps  %xmm4,%xmm0                D += helper
    mulps  0x70(%r11),%xmm4     high: *= S2's slot   -- memory
    addps  0x50(%r11),%xmm4           += D's slot    -- memory

`TWO_HELPERS` is keyed by shape and forces two for every `lanereg3`, which is right
for every other mnemonic wearing it -- two sources loaded into two registers. The
FMA case is carved out there, because asking for a second helper is exactly what
cost the memory form 66 windows before `span_slot_op` existed.

231 is again the ordering that needs a scratch for its low half, the destination
being the ADDEND; 213 and 132 multiply in place.

#### The fixture caught what every counter called a success

First run of the register form: **5 built, 0 refused, 0 VEX left in `.text`, and
the program returned 29.** The stub held `66 0f 38 b8 (bad)` -- Finding 263's exact
failure -- because the new branch sat AFTER the ordinary `lanereg3` branch in the
if-chain and never ran.

Every number the tool printed said success. The refusal table said zero, the VEX
count said zero, and the image was broken. **Only running it found this**, and it
is the second time in one pass: Finding 300's own emitter refused 66 windows while
reporting a clean build.

`check-shadow-pe` now gates six FMA fixtures -- `fmamem`, `fma231`, `fma132`,
`fmareg`, `fmareg213`, `fmareg132` -- one per ordering per shape, each reading lane
0 from the low half and lanes 4 and 7 from the upper, and each required to answer
29 with `--shadow-regs=off` so that a fixture which never needed permanent slots
cannot pass for the wrong reason.

#### What is left of the family

69 sites: `vfmaddsub`/`vfmsubadd`, where Finding 4 measured that a plain
multiply-add computes the WRONG THING for half the lanes -- a correctness bug, not
a precision one -- and the four-operand shapes. Those stay refused deliberately.

### Finding 300 -- the census buckets are a dependency graph, and FMA lowers in a span

Findings 298 and 299 each ended by calling a class a floor, and the survey they
produced treats the buckets as independent. They are not.

    903 distinct surviving readers blame the 1,136 withheld windows:
      553  kept: its window was withheld          61%
      197  declined: no SSE form at any register  22%   -- the FMA class
       71  256-bit: arithmetic rather than a copy
       41  lost to an overlap or a refused stub
       29  never a candidate
       10  not in the frontier at all

A window is withheld because a surviving 256-bit instruction still reads an upper
half it would stop zeroing -- and every surviving instruction is itself a frontier
site with its own reason. **61% of the class blames itself**, so it is a feedback
structure rather than 1,227 independent losses. And the FMA floor is not a 208-site
floor: it holds windows hostage too.

That is why this item was picked. 208 was written off twice on its size, and size
was the wrong measure.

#### The leverage claim, and how far it held

Recording which reader blamed which window: of 1,136 dropped windows carrying 2,889
edges, **283 are blamed ONLY by FMA-class readers** and would have no blamer left
if that class lowered. Against the 113-site item this displaced -- worth forty to
sixty -- 208 plus 283 was an order of magnitude better.

**The realised figure is 67 sites and zero windows.**

    frontier                                  2,346 -> 2,279
      declined: no SSE form at any register     208 -> 158
      never a candidate                          54 ->  44
      kept: its window was withheld           1,227 -> 1,224

Not one window was released. Releasing one needs EVERY reader blaming it lowered,
and only the memory-source FMAs do; the 71 register-only sites remain and are
evidently spread across those windows rather than concentrated. **A class-level
count cannot support a claim that needs a per-window conjunction**, which is the
same error as counting refusals and calling them sites -- and it survived being
written down as an edge list, because the edges were right and the inference over
them was not.

#### What was built

`vfmadd{132,213,231}{ps,pd}` with a memory source now lowers in the span path, as a
multiply and an add per half. NOT bit-exact -- two roundings replace one -- which
extends Finding 4's recorded deviation rather than making a new one.
`vfmaddsub`/`vfmsubadd` stay refused, and that is not an oversight: Finding 4
measured that a plain multiply-add sequence computes the WRONG THING for half the
lanes, a correctness bug rather than a precision one.

Finding 263 refuses every FMA whatever its shape, and that argument is about
NARROWING: `lanemem` is emitted as `movaps` then the opcode, which for an FMA is
`66 0f 38 a8` and decodes to nothing. A sequence is not a narrowing, so the door
opens for exactly the population that has an emitter. **Both guard sites had to
open together** -- 263 says so in as many words -- or the collector builds a window
the emitter then refuses.

#### Two wrong turns, both mine, both found by reading the tool's own output

**A second helper that cost more than the emitter won.** The first version loaded
the destination's upper half AND the first source's into registers, and refused 66
windows for `FMA member wants a second helper` -- more than it lowered. A slot is
memory and an SSE arithmetic instruction takes memory as its source; only a MOVE
needs a register. Reading the other slot by address costs one register instead of
two and the refusal went to zero.

    movups 0x50(%r11),%xmm4      h = D's slot
    mulps  0x60(%r11),%xmm4      h *= S1's slot -- read, not loaded
    addps  0x10(%rax),%xmm4      + mem[16:32]
    movups %xmm4,0x50(%r11)

**And "fix the routing" was a wrong diagnosis.** The first Starfield run gained 25
sites, and the reading was that the sites never reach the span path because the
collector declines them. They do reach it: `needs_sequence` has exempted FMA from
the collector's 256-bit decline since Finding 90. What was actually happening is
the 66 above, in code twenty minutes old. **The refusal table naming my own string
beside the tool's is the only reason it was visible.**

#### The fixtures, and what they are built to fail

There was no 256-bit FMA fixture at all -- only a scalar `vfmadd213ss`. `fmamem`,
`fma231` and `fma132` are one per ordering, each reading back lane 0 from the low
half and lanes 4 and 7 from the upper, because a fixture checking only lane 0 would
pass a lowering that narrows the low half and drops the high one, which is how this
shape is likeliest to break.

They sit in `check-shadow-pe`, which runs each with `--shadow-regs=off` as well and
requires it NOT to answer 77: a fixture that is right without permanent slots never
needed them. All three give 29 without and 77 with.

**Testing 231 was not box-ticking.** It is the largest group at 93 sites and the one
ordering whose low half has the destination as the ADDEND, so the product needs
somewhere to live and borrows `helper`; 213 and 132 multiply in place and need no
scratch. A fixture for 213 alone would have left the biggest case untested.

`verify` passes: the stub decodes -- the check Finding 263 exists for -- and no
surviving 256-bit read takes a stale upper half, which is the one that would catch a
wrong slot address in the new arithmetic.

#### What is left of the class

71 register-only sites, `vfmadd231ps %ymm3,%ymm2,%ymm4`. Three ymm operands means
the upper half wants D's slot, S1's slot and S2's slot at once -- and with the
slot-as-memory form, two of the three are addresses, so it may want no more
registers than the memory form does. Until those lower, the 283 leverage claim
cannot be tested.

### Finding 299 -- the frontier's last big classes are floors, and a table with two denominators

Finding 298 closed the repair. This is the survey of what was under it, and the
answer is that nothing above a hundred sites is open.

    2,346 surviving VEX
      kept: its window was withheld                  1,227   Finding 298: 550 a floor,
                                                             586 a measured negative
      declined: outside .pdata                         319   documented trade
      declined: next instruction is a branch target    228   sandwiched, see below
      declined: no SSE form at any register            208   the FMA family, Finding 263
      declined: next instruction will not move         106
      declined: 256-bit: arithmetic rather than a copy  84
      lost to an overlap or a refused stub              83
      never a candidate                                 54
      kept: a repair left it in VEX form                27

**`outside .pdata` is not the 16,256 its own tool's docstring records.**
`outside.leaf_ranges` has been wired in since it was written and took the class to
319; what is left contains `(bad)` or runs off the end, and `outside.py` keeps those
refused on purpose -- "being slightly less effective is the right price for not
corrupting data". A floor by decision, not by omission.

#### A bucket named for the first blocker

A site under five bytes cannot carry a `jmp rel32`, so its window widens forward over
the next instruction and, failing that, backward over the previous one. The backward
fallback's six refusals were all bare `pass`, so the reason reaching `declined` was
always the forward one. Counting the pair:

    next instruction is a branch target  then the site itself is one   206
    next instruction will not move       then previous will not move   113
    next instruction is a branch target  then previous will not move    14
    next instruction is a branch target  then previous falls through    13
    next instruction will not move       then the site itself is one     5

It reconciles against a count taken in another pass: the forward halves are 233 and
118 where the census reports 228 and 106 surviving, and the difference of 17 is the
census's own `of those, swallowed anyway 17`.

**206 are sandwiched** -- the next instruction is branched to so widening forward
buries it, the site is branched to so widening backward buries that. Scalar
three-operand arithmetic whose destination differs from its first source, so the SSE
form wants an extra `movaps` and does not fit in place either.

**The trampoline was measured rather than built.** A 2-byte `jmp rel8` over the site
into inter-function `int3` padding holding a `jmp rel32` is the standard escape.
Starfield has 160,084 padding runs of five or more bytes and 1.6 MB of them -- and
only **28 of 228 (12%)** have any within `rel8` reach. A mechanism for 28 sites is
not a mechanism. One measurement, no implementation, which is Finding 298's lesson
applied a step earlier.

#### A table whose two halves counted different populations

`moved_instruction` has taken a `reasons` Counter since Finding 88 and `build_stub`
has passed one all along; the two widening call sites passed nothing. Wiring them up
is an interface only as wired as its least-used method -- and the unused caller was
the one covering the class in question.

The first version counted forward reasons at the attempt and backward reasons at the
decline, and printed them adjacent under one heading:

    forward   the aliased form has no usable scratch    289      <- attempts
    backward  no direct SSE form and not a sequence      49      <- outcomes

Forward widening is tried at EVERY short site and most go on to succeed backward, so
the forward rows described a population an order of magnitude larger. Held in a local
and folded in at the decline, both halves are about declined sites:

    over 118 declined site(s) whose forward move was refused, and 127 whose backward was
      backward  no direct SSE form and not a sequence     49
      forward   256-bit, no Y strategy took it            46
      forward   no direct SSE form and not a sequence     46
      backward  256-bit, no Y strategy took it            40
      backward  the aliased form has no usable scratch    38
      forward   the aliased form has no usable scratch    26

46+46+26 = 118 and 49+40+38 = 127, to the unit.

**The correction is eleven-fold on the largest row** -- `the aliased form has no
usable scratch` was 289 and is 26 -- and `vblendv would not lower`, at 107, is
**absent**: every one of those sites succeeded backward. The four biggest rows were
almost entirely sites the tool went on to handle.

**What caught it was not that 647 looked wrong.** It looked like a plausible large
number. It was that the backward half reconciled to the unit and the forward half did
not, against a count taken elsewhere. A bare total with no stated population is what
let it hide, so the denominator is printed now, with the note that one refusal may
give several reasons -- rows summing past the site count is then correct rather than
an error, and a reader can tell the two apart.

#### Where this leaves the frontier

Every class above a hundred is a floor. The largest that is not is the 113, whose
three reasons are `no direct SSE form and not a sequence`, `256-bit, no Y strategy
took it`, and `the aliased form has no usable scratch`. Solving it entirely is worth
on the order of forty to sixty sites against 2,346.

### Finding 298 -- splitting a dropped window recovers windows and loses sites

Finding 297 left the stale-read repair holding half the frontier: 1,177 of 2,346
surviving sites sat in windows the repair withheld. The drop total is the wrong
number to work from, because it cannot tell a window with no ladder behind it from
one that walked every rung and found each blamed. Those want opposite work.

    unit           every alternative covers a blamed producer   1,036 win   4,215 sites
    unit           no alternative window exists                    97 win     184
    (no strategy)  no alternative window exists                     3 win       3

**91% of the loss is an exhausted ladder, not a missing one**, and the baseline is
the same shape at 90% -- 623 of 693 -- so this is the binary rather than anything
Finding 297 introduced. Giving the other strategies a ladder is worth 100 windows
of 1,136.

**The site column is exposure and not loss.** It counts every VEX instruction lying
inside a dropped extent; the census attributes 1,177 surviving sites to this class,
the difference being sites another window or an in-place patch picks up anyway.

#### What the ladder could not say, and what it cost to find out

Every rung `unit_shortening` offers is a contiguous run anchored at one site, so it
can shorten a window and widen it backwards and cannot express one that starts past
a producer in the middle. Cutting each dropped window at the producers it was blamed
for leaves a piece still holding a VEX site in **586 of 1,136**.

Anchoring the ladder at every site the window covers reaches those pieces. The
frontier got **worse**:

    VEX in the rewritten .text        2,346      2,349
      refused, stub not buildable       190        243     +53
      in a window the repair dropped  1,177      1,047    -130
      skipped for overlap                13         26     +13
      unaccounted                         0         67     +67

134 fewer windows were dropped and three more sites survived. It recovered 130 sites
and gave back 53 to stubs that would not build and 13 to overlap -- the pieces being
smaller and more numerous -- with 67 the census could no longer attribute, which is
Finding 282's substituted-start blind spot arriving by a new route. `verify` passed
throughout: the image was correct and worse.

**A window is not a unit of loss, and this item was picked off a window count.** The
586 was also an upper bound measured against round-one blame; by the time the loop
settled, `no gap holds a site` had risen 547 -> 750, so two thirds of the opportunity
was eaten by the repair's own cascade rather than by unbuildable stubs.

Reverted, and the revert is proved rather than asserted: byte-identical image, 1,136
dropped, every split restored.

#### The revert control found the real defect

    default build          56 rounds,   693 windows dropped
    --teb-scratch=auto     56 rounds, 1,136 windows dropped
    REPAIR_ROUNDS = 64

`REPAIR_ROUNDS` was documented as "headroom over a measured 15, not a second guess".
**It is 56.** The 15 was taken when `--shadow-regs=all` was new and did not survive
the two default flips after it, so the shipping default was eight rounds from the
bound -- and the far side of that bound is not a worse image but a refusal to build
anything, which this session tripped for real at 103 rounds.

Nothing could have shown the margin closing, because the decay the comment quoted
lived in a session and not in the tool. `REPAIR_DECAY` is that trace and it prints.

Two facts the old number lacked. **The round count belongs to the binary, not the
flags**: the two runs above share their last 41 rounds value for value, the same
stubborn windows in both, so turning a flag off buys no margin. And **the decay is
not monotone** -- it rises 17 times on the way down as each substitution creates
fresh blame -- so no safe bound is extrapolable from the early rounds.

256 now, and the tool warns when the rounds used pass half of it. Both halves were
made to fire: a cap of 8 refuses naming 440 dropped, a cap of 1 refuses on the
fixture, and a cap of 100 prints the warning, exits 0, and writes an image
byte-identical to the one built at 256 -- so the guard guards without changing
output. The warning is unreachable from `pe-repairdrop`, which settles in one round:
firing it needs the rounds used above half the cap while still settling, and one
round cannot satisfy both.

#### What is left, measured

550 of the 1,136 dropped windows are a floor: cut them at every producer they were
blamed for and no surviving piece holds a VEX site at all, so there is nothing to
place either side. That is measured now rather than assumed.

### Finding 297 -- the TEB route is built, and the wall it was written against is gone

Finding 296 measured away the precondition; this is the route itself. `--teb-scratch=auto`
asks the process for its scratch bytes instead of naming an offset in somebody else's TEB,
which is the open half Finding 280 left. The same TLS callback that fills the index in calls
`TlsAlloc` twice through the image's own IAT and patches two more tables of displacements.

    unconditional lowering              base       auto
    sites asked about                 36,903     36,138
    built                             34,382     35,532
    refused                            2,521        606
      no dead GPR and no home space    1,878          -

The 1,878 were served by **279 stubs** -- 1,116 displacements, four per stub, being the save
and the restore of each of two borrowed registers. Regions improved with them: not
representable 44 -> 9, refused after the walk said yes 45 -> 4. `verify` passes on the
result, and the check that matters saw its subject rather than sleeping through it: *no call
inside any of 279 TEB save bracket(s)*, the same 279 the apply reported.

    VEX in the rewritten .text        2,687     2,346
      declined by the collector       1,825       955      -870
      refused, stub not buildable       122       190       +68
      in a window the repair dropped    694     1,177      +483
      in-place patch reverted            37        11       -26
      skipped for overlap                 9        13        +4
      unaccounted                         0         0

**The frontier is 2,346, and half of what is left is now one class.** 870 sites came out of
`declined` and 483 went straight into `dropped`, because serving a site builds a window and a
window that swallows a VEX.128 write whose zeroing is still read does not get placed. The net
is 341. What the route actually did was move the largest remaining class from one the tool
refuses outright to one the stale-read repair might yet recover, and the repair is now the
whole game: 1,177 of 2,346.

**The first census of this said 679 and it was measured wrong.** It was run without
